title: Establish Claude Captain and Codex Captain persistent agent seats
description:
OBJECTIVE

Give the two long-lived Eshyra coding agents durable organizational identities -
Claude Captain and Codex Captain - occupied by disposable model sessions.
A Captain is a durable seat; "main session" is only a harness/runtime
classification and one eligibility condition for occupying a seat.

NOT the in-game Dungeon Master seat. eshyra-plwe owns persistent DM-seat
reconstruction inside the Eshyra product; this bead owns the development-agent
harness seats and must stay separate from it.

FOUR SEPARATE CATEGORIES (the design must not merge them)

1. Standing seat identity / charter - long-lived role and operating behavior
   that survives context resets, CLI restarts, and compatible model upgrades.
2. Repository/task authority - AGENTS.md, ADRs, owning beads, findings, exact
   implementation, Git/PR state. Authoritative; always reread and revalidated.
3. Advisory predecessor handoff - unfinished cognitive state, hypotheses,
   salient next investigation, references to active beads/branches/PRs/
   dispatches. NOT authority.
4. Transient runtime session - occupant harness, model, session id, time.
   Occupant metadata only; seat identity must not depend on it, and seat
   history must never be read as inherited capability.

Invariant: the seat remembers how to work; repository systems remember what is
true; the handoff remembers what was happening.

SCOPE

- A Claude Captain charter and a Codex Captain charter, each bounded, stored as
  personal user-local content, never as tracked repository authority.
- Per-seat advisory handoffs that do not share one mutable store, resolve
  identically from every worktree of the same clone, and are untracked.
- Technical routing that decides which prompt material reaches which context.
  Gating must be structural, never a prose request to ignore text.
- Permanent regression evidence for the routing and handoff boundaries.

VISIBILITY MATRIX TO PROVE

- General repository authority reaches every agent, unchanged.
- Claude Captain identity reaches only authorized Claude Captain occupants.
- The existing privileged Claude supervisor overlay keeps its current gate and
  reaches no other context - not Sonnet, not Claude subagents, not Codex
  Captain, not dispatched Codex workers.
- Codex Captain identity reaches a direct Codex Captain session only, and not a
  Claude-dispatched Codex worker or a Codex-native subagent.
- Each Captain sees only its own handoff; dispatched children see neither.

KNOWN CONSTRAINT (measured, not assumed)

codex exec fires SessionStart. A Codex SessionStart event is therefore NOT
proof of Codex Captain occupancy, because dispatch-codex.sh launches workers
through codex exec. The discriminator must be an explicit durable launch
identity, not model name, cwd, bead title, branch name, or permission mode.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

1. Owning bead exists and carries the design; no duplicate seat bead created.
2. Both charters exist, are bounded, and are stored outside tracked repository
   source.
3. Claude Captain injection is gated to an authorized main Claude session and
   fails closed on unknown/absent model identity, on subagents, and on
   malformed hook input.
4. The privileged supervisor overlay stays out of AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, bead
   descriptions, and bd memories, and its gate is unchanged.
5. Codex Captain injection is unreachable from the dispatch launch path by
   construction, with defense-in-depth checks on top.
6. dispatch-codex.sh marks its children explicitly as dispatched implementation
   workers, and every existing safety property and default of that launcher is
   preserved.
7. Handoffs are advisory: startup material requires reconciliation of any
   handoff claim against current beads, Git, PR, and dispatch/process state
   before acting, and correctness never depends on a graceful-shutdown hook.
8. Missing, stale, or corrupt seat state degrades to ordinary repository
   behavior rather than blocking work.
9. Repo-local regression tests execute the real routing scripts against
   representative hook payloads and prove the matrix above.
10. Hard-reset smoke evidence for both seats, plus proof that a dispatched
    worker receives neither Captain identity nor supervisor policy.
11. npm run verify:worktree passes; work lands by PR per AGENTS.md.

NON-GOALS

Not a multi-agent framework, agent ontology, reputation system, capability
ledger, or cross-agent shared memory. Not a reverse Codex-to-Claude dispatch
system. Not a replacement for AGENTS.md, ADRs, or beads as the inter-agent task
protocol. Not a reason to widen the audience of the privileged supervisor
policy.
notes:
PR #527 opened 2026-09-07 from branch eshyra-kusc (head f39d089): https://github.com/jbongaarts/eshyra/pull/527 . Per AGENTS.md this bead stays in_progress until that PR merges.

Architecture: three composed layers (personal charter + live repository authority + advisory handoff), only the middle one authoritative. Claude Captain gated by the existing fail-closed main-session gate (no agent_id, not a resume, supervisor-class model). Codex Captain gated by CONFIG LAYER: measured that codex exec fires SessionStart identically to an interactive session, so the seat hook is registered only in the eshyra-captain profile overlay that the dispatch path never loads; ESHYRA_SEAT_ROLE/ESHYRA_DISPATCH_CHILD are defence in depth, not the boundary. Privileged supervisor overlay untouched, same gate and audience.

Storage: charters user-local and untracked; handoffs at <git common dir>/eshyra-seats/<seat>/handoff.md so every worktree of a clone resolves the same file while git status stays clean.

Child eshyra-itnm closed. 22 regression tests; verify:worktree green (4943 passed, 20 documented skips). Live smoke evidence recorded on the PR for both seats and for a dispatched worker.

OPEN ITEM with a concrete owner (me, on this bead): Codex hook trust has not been granted interactively yet - smoke tests used --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust. First real codex-captain launch prompts once; until then Codex skips the hook silently. seat:install --check infers trust by finding the shim path in ~/.codex/config.toml because the trust hash scheme could not be derived; confirm that inference against a genuinely trusted hook.
REVIEW #5565764326 (head f39d089) REPAIRED at head 2951fb2. All three blocking findings fixed.

F1 (material trust-boundary): CONFIRMED and repaired. Codex runs command hooks OUTSIDE its sandbox (its own prompt says so: 'Hooks can run outside the sandbox after you trust them') and trust covers the declaration, not the transitive closure. The shim resolved the seat script from the active worktree, so any branch or any dispatched worker able to write repo files could gain unsandboxed user-level execution at the next Captain startup with no new prompt. Closure is now user-local: installer copies seat runtime + library into ~/.codex/seats/, trusted shim execs only that fixed path. Negative regression poisons BOTH the entrypoint and a transitive dependency in the repo and proves the installed hook output is unchanged, and that --check reports the drift. The prior test that pinned the unsafe property was removed.

F2 (trust reporting): CONFIRMED and repaired, with the open trust item now CLOSED by real evidence. Completed a genuine first-launch trust grant through the interactive prompt with NO --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust, then measured where Codex records it. Ground truth (Codex 0.153.4): trust is keyed by the DECLARING file plus event and group/handler indices - here /home/jhbongaarts/.codex/eshyra-captain.config.toml:session_start:0:0 - and is written back INTO THAT PROFILE FILE, not into ~/.codex/config.toml. The old heuristic therefore reported a genuinely trusted hook as untrusted. Fixed to the real key in the real file. This exposed a further defect the review did not name: the installer compared and rewrote the profile byte-for-byte, so every reinstall DESTROYED the trust record Codex writes there; it now owns the hook declaration only and leaves [hooks.state] intact. Verified: reinstall preserves trusted_hash and the hook still fires unbypassed. --check now reports trusted/untrusted/stale/unknown and exits non-zero when untrusted. The hash algorithm is not derivable, but it is not needed: trust was granted for the exact declaration text, so a byte-matching declaration is still the trusted one, and a hand-edited one reports 'differs' and is rewritten, which is exactly when Codex re-prompts.

F3 (producer evidence): repaired. scripts/seats/check-dispatch-markers.mjs verifies both markers are set AND that they reach the child process rather than staying in the parent, with fixture coverage (env-prefix form, export form, each marker missing, wrong role value, parent-only assignment, digest determinism). Real-artifact controls: PASS on the current launcher, FAIL on the pre-change backup dispatch-codex.sh.bak.20260907T000837 with both markers reported missing. Current launcher digest sha256:308a4280a12a71549d9d71836b7939d98e91c6b7c4d91d6f137c0962f6e1655e; --baseline pins it so unrelated edits are caught. The checker takes the launcher path as an argument and carries no dispatch policy, so it exposes no supervisor-only instructions.

Also fixed install-on-import: the installer's main block executed on import, so importing it from a test performed a real install against $HOME.

verify:worktree green at 2951fb2 (4946 passed, 20 documented skips). Live smoke re-run after the repair: hook fires with NO bypass flag and the seat answers 'Codex Captain; no, a predecessor handoff is advisory, not authority.'

KNOWN AND DELIBERATELY NOT CHANGED: the Claude-side hook runs repo code via .claude/settings.json. That is Claude Code's existing project-trust model, predates this PR, and is the same posture as the pre-existing supervisor hook; changing it would require fighting the harness and is not authorized by this bead. Flagged for the reviewer rather than silently ignored.
RE-REVIEW #5566119556 (head 2951fb2) REPAIRED at head c702e90. Prior F1 closed by the reviewer. Two remaining findings fixed; both had one root cause - inferring a runtime property from static text instead of observing it.

F2: Codex runs a hook only when enabled AND stored trusted_hash == its computed current_hash. The old checker read neither, and its test asserted a fabricated 'sha256:x' was trusted. Tried the reviewer's preferred route and both paths closed: (a) hooks/list is authoritative and exposes key/enabled/currentHash/trustStatus - confirmed working against trusted project hooks in another repo - but returns [] for a PROFILE-declared hook, and app-server rejects --profile ('--profile only applies to runtime commands and codex mcp'); declaring the hook anywhere hooks/list can reach would put it in a layer dispatched workers load, destroying the boundary. (b) The hash is not reproducible: brute-forced canonical-JSON encodings over the exact normalized field set hooks/list exposes for hooks whose hashes are known, no match; mirroring undocumented normalization would rot on any Codex upgrade.
RESOLUTION: stop inferring. The installed shim stamps ~/.codex/seats/.last-run whenever Codex actually dispatches the hook; the installer clears it whenever it rewrites the declaration or the shim. An observed run proves the CURRENT declaration executes, subsuming missing hash, stale hash, enabled=false, identity-changing sibling fields, and Codex upgrades. State entry now parsed, not substring-matched. --check exits non-zero for untrusted/disabled/stale/unverified/unknown. Demonstrated on the real install: reinstall -> 'unverified' exit 1; one real codex-captain session -> 'trusted (observed running 2026-09-07T06:58:06Z)' exit 0.

F3: the static checker was unsound - it PASSED a launcher that exported both markers then unset them before launch. DELETED rather than kept (an unsound predicate in the tree is a trap). Replaced by scripts/seats/probe-dispatch-markers.mjs, which runs the real launcher in a disposable sandbox with codex replaced by a stub that records its own environment, and asserts the exact values the child received. Reviewer's counterexample now reproduced as permanent evidence: OLD PASS exit 0, NEW FAIL exit 1 with both markers null. Also covers a wrong-value launcher whose only 'dispatched-worker' string is in a comment, and a launcher that never reaches a child. --baseline proves the launcher differs from its pre-change copy only by marker injection (catches a dropped guard and an unrelated smuggled line). Real artifact: PASS on ~/.claude/dispatch-codex.sh, digest sha256:308a4280a12a71549d9d71836b7939d98e91c6b7c4d91d6f137c0962f6e1655e.

Self-review of this head (not reviewer-reported) additionally fixed: a poll loop shelling out to sleep, and a set-based baseline diff that would call a duplicated-then-removed line unchanged.

verify:worktree green at c702e90 (4947 passed, 20 documented skips).
BOUNDED VERIFICATION #5575403400 (head c702e90) REPAIRED at head d9993dc. Prior F1 remains closed.

F2 (observation not bound to state): all three counterexamples reproduced against the live installation before the fix - valid-but-wrong trusted_hash, 'timeout = 30' added after statusMessage inside the handler table, and a changed Codex build - each left the bare timestamp intact while Codex would classify the hook Modified. FIX: the .last-run stamp now records the IDENTITY of what ran: sha256 over (hook declaration tables + the [hooks.state.<key>] entry) plus the Codex binary identity (realpath:size:mtime, overridable via ESHYRA_SEAT_CODEX_ID for tests). --check re-derives it and reports 'superseded' on mismatch. Unrelated tables Codex writes into the same profile (tui.model_availability_nux) are excluded so ordinary churn cannot invalidate a good observation - pinned by test. Live evidence: all three counterexamples now 'superseded' exit 1; required lifecycle rerun with NO bypass flag - reinstall that rewrites the shim -> 'unverified' exit 1, one real codex-captain session -> 'trusted (observed running 2026-09-07T20:46:13.977Z)' exit 0.

F3 (baseline proof unsound): counted multiset discarded sequence and admitted any added line merely containing a marker token. FIX: diffAgainstBaseline now walks both files as ORDERED programs - removing authorized additions must leave the baseline byte-for-byte - and an added line qualifies only if it is a comment or mentions a marker while assigning nothing but marker names. Reviewer's counterexamples are permanent tests: guard moved after the launch, and 'MODEL=opus # ESHYRA_SEAT_ROLE', plus an outright removed guard. Real launcher still PASSES both the child-environment probe and the ordered baseline comparison, which is now the actual preservation evidence rather than the digest standing in for it.

RESIDUAL ON THE RECORD: the added-line predicate accepts a line whose only assignments are markers even if it also runs a command - the real launcher's --dry-run printf line is exactly that shape, which is why the rule permits it. Tightening further would be guesswork about a file this check does not own; the ordered byte-exact remainder plus the runtime probe is what constrains it. Disclosed on the PR.

PROCESS DEFECT OF MY OWN, worth remembering: the first F2 signature change silently no-opped because Biome had reformatted the function since I last read it and I used a plain string replace with no assertion. The checker reported 'unverified' against a correct stamp until traced. Assert on every scripted edit.

verify:worktree green at d9993dc (4948 passed, 20 documented skips).
CLOSURE REVIEW #5575560785 (head d9993dc) REPAIRED at head d87cfba. Prior F1 closed.

F2 (identity not bound to the executing runtime): correct. codexBinaryIdentity fingerprinted realpath:size:mtime of the PATH 'codex'. For the npm CLI that is bin/codex.js, a launcher that resolves a separate platform package and spawns its native binary - byte-identical launcher, different executing build. Also 'unresolved' was a STABLE identity that could keep one observation trusted across every upgrade. FIX: renamed to codexRuntimeIdentity, anchored on the runtime's own report (codex --version; measured ~190ms, confirmed it does not itself fire hooks), resolved entry kept only as secondary signal, and FAILS CLOSED - unidentifiable runtime returns null and gets its own terminal state 'runtime-unknown' that never compares equal. Regression exercises the REAL resolver (one stub launcher file, byte-identical across runs, reporting two different versions = the npm wrapper case), plus missing codex and a codex that cannot report a version.

F3 (permissive grammar): correct, and the reviewer rightly refused my disclosed residual - a documented escape hatch is still an escape hatch. All three named siblings were real: 'ESHYRA_SEAT_ROLE=dispatched-worker touch /tmp/x', 'touch $ESHYRA_SEAT_ROLE', and '#!/bin/sh' inserted above the real shebang. FIX: grammar removed entirely. Preservation is proven against an EXACT ordered patch - literal added lines in hunks, each anchored to the baseline line it follows - stored in-repo at scripts/seats/dispatch-marker-patch.txt so the authorized external change is reviewable in the PR diff. Removing exactly those hunks must leave the baseline byte-for-byte at the intended location. The dry-run printf change is now one explicitly authorized hunk. --authorize re-derives the patch after an intentional launcher change; routine verification pins to it.

Live evidence: lifecycle with no bypass flag - reinstall rewriting the shim -> 'unverified' exit 1, one real Captain session -> 'trusted (observed running 2026-09-07T21:03:49.153Z)' exit 0. Real launcher PASSES both the child-environment probe and the pinned patch; refused: all three command-injection siblings, a removed guard, a changed default, and the block moved to another anchor.

SELF-FOUND on this head: the first cut of the removal diagnostic reported 'baseline line removed' for the UNCHANGED launcher because a duplicated baseline line satisfied its lookahead - caught by running the unchanged file as a control before trusting the counterexamples. Authorized match is now attempted before any diagnosis.

verify:worktree green at d87cfba (4949 passed, 20 documented skips).
EXHAUSTIVE CLOSURE AUDIT #5575701184 (head d87cfba) REPAIRED at head 60df37f. Four batched failure modes, all continuations of F2/F3. Prior F1 closed.

F2-A (profile not semantically owned): currentMatches/hookTrustState accepted the profile on a SUBSTRING while hard-coding state key session_start:0:0. Codex keys state by the handler's real group/handler indices, so a prepended SessionStart group moves the managed handler off 0:0 and the checker reads a sibling's state. Same hole admitted extra fields on the managed handler - 'async = true' is the sharp one: Codex then schedules the hook separately and EXCLUDES it from the results whose stdout becomes additional_contexts, so the runtime still executes and stamps while NO Captain context is injected. FIX: ownership is now the whole hook-declaration region compared exactly (all [[hooks.*]]/[hooks.*] tables except [hooks.state]); unrelated tables still ignored. Live: async=true -> stale exit 1; prepended sibling group -> stale exit 1.

F2-B (test seam live in production): codexRuntimeIdentity honoured ESHYRA_SEAT_CODEX_ID unconditionally; the installed hook inherits the ambient environment, so an inherited value freezes the runtime half of the identity and defeats upgrade invalidation. FIX: honoured only alongside ESHYRA_SEAT_TEST_ROOT. Regression proves an inherited value cannot mask a real version change.

F3-A (anchor not bound to an occurrence) and F3-B (baseline not pinned): both closed by ONE change - verification is now by RECONSTRUCTION. The patch pins the pre-change baseline digest (checked first) and each hunk carries the baseline line INDEX; pinned baseline + exact hunks at exact indices must reproduce the launcher byte-for-byte. Strictly stronger than the ordered walk, which survives only for legible diagnostics. Live: tampered baseline refused by digest before any content comparison; duplicate-anchor move refused (permanent test with a repeated ANCHOR line).

Reviewer deliberately did NOT elevate explicit-install replacement of the user-local seat runtime/library - the explicit install is the authorization and Codex's trust sits on the unchanged shim declaration by design. Agreed and recorded.

verify:worktree green at 60df37f (4952 passed, 20 documented skips). Lifecycle with no bypass flag -> trusted (observed running 2026-09-07T21:46:47.887Z).
FRESH FULL SUBSYSTEM REVIEW #5576014927 (head 60df37f) REPAIRED at head b1466f9. Three findings, all accepted.

F2-C (bypassed run forges trust evidence): --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust runs enabled hooks WITHOUT persisted trust, and the runtime stamped on execution alone, so a valid-format but stale trusted_hash could go superseded, be laundered by one bypassed run, and read 'trusted' while the next ordinary session silently got no Captain context. FIX: the runtime is exec'd by the shim, so its parent process IS the Codex process and its argv carries the admission flags (verified empirically by walking /proc ancestry from inside a live hook). Only 'persisted-trust' admission stamps; 'unknown' stamps nothing; the wrapper refuses to forward the flag. Live: stale hash -> superseded exit 1; bypassed run -> STILL superseded, stamp untouched; normal run -> trusted exit 0; wrapper refuses the flag exit 1.

F4 (primary boundary unverified at the producer): probeLauncher recorded only child ENV, so a launcher running 'codex -p eshyra-captain exec ...' would pass with correct markers while the PRIMARY structural boundary (a dispatched worker never loads the Captain profile) was broken and the Captain hook ran in a worker. FIX: stub records argv too; probe refuses any Captain-profile selection in all three flag spellings; probe exercises 5 launch-producing option paths (default, --model, --effort, --sandbox, combined). Negative control launcher with correct markers but -p eshyra-captain is now FAILED.

F3-C (proof hole relocated into the evidence): the patch regression asserted only that each authorized line mentioned a marker token - the same defect removed from the verifier, moved into its evidence, satisfied by 'touch /tmp/x $CHILD'. FIX: tracked patch pinned to its EXACT approved content (literal hunks and lines), so any widening changes the test and forces explicit review.

SELF-FOUND on this head, and worse than the bug it was fixing: the first cut of the admission change applied its call site but NOT its import, because the import block had been reformatted since I last read it. hookAdmission was undefined, the hook CRASHED on every session, and the seat silently stopped injecting while --check still read 'trusted' from the previous stamp. Caught by noticing the stamp timestamp had stopped advancing. Second occurrence in this PR of a reformatted region silently swallowing an edit. Also fixed: admission matched the flag as a SUBSTRING, so an unrelated ancestor command line or a prompt argument containing the flag text would read as bypassed - now an exact argv match with a test.

MERGED. PR #527 merged 2026-09-07T22:19:55Z as merge commit 43adf2b (reviewed head b1466f9); all CI green. Closing per AGENTS.md now that the PR has landed.

Delivered: Claude Captain and Codex Captain as durable seats occupied by disposable model sessions.
- Claude Captain: repo SessionStart hook, gated to an authorized main session (no agent_id, not a resume, supervisor-class model); fails closed on unknown/absent model identity and on subagents. claude -p sends no model field so print mode never occupies the seat.
- Codex Captain: gated by CONFIG LAYER - the hook is registered only in the ~/.codex/eshyra-captain.config.toml profile overlay, which the dispatch path never loads. ESHYRA_SEAT_ROLE/ESHYRA_DISPATCH_CHILD are defence in depth.
- Storage: charters user-local and untracked (~/.claude/seats/, ~/.codex/seats/); handoffs at <git common dir>/eshyra-seats/<seat>/handoff.md so every worktree resolves the same file while git status stays clean.
- Trust: the trusted Codex hook executes only user-local code pinned by explicit install; trust is proven by an OBSERVED run bound to the declaration, its persisted trust state, and the Codex runtime, and only when Codex admitted the run under normal persisted trust (a --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust run cannot launder a stale hash).
- Dispatcher: verified by reconstruction from a pinned pre-change baseline plus an exact authorized patch (scripts/seats/dispatch-marker-patch.txt), with the child's ENV and ARGV both asserted at the real producer across 5 launch modes.

OPERATIONAL DEPENDENCY, do not delete: ~/.claude/dispatch-codex.sh.bak.20260907T000837 is the pinned pre-change baseline whose digest sha256:6436a04c... is recorded in dispatch-marker-patch.txt. Removing it breaks 'npm run seat:install'-adjacent launcher verification (probe-dispatch-markers.mjs --baseline). Re-derive with --authorize if the launcher is intentionally changed.
